correctness.rationale: For a nonempty induced biclique subgraph, the same-side relation on its vertex set is equality or nonadjacency, so an isomorphism either respects the occupied sides or swaps them. This also works for singleton and edgeless domains. The global degrees differ if a>b, so only the sparse within-side bijections extend, each by completing a permutation on each side; their independent choices multiply to R_aR_b. A swap consists of independent partial injections A→B and B→A with at least one nonempty, giving (1+C)^2−1. The coefficients of C are positive in every rank 1,…,b, so N has positive support 1,…,2b, and its leading coefficient is the square of binom(a,b)b!. For a=b both global orientations occur, yielding 2R_a²−1 with the empty map counted once. Independent direct enumeration of actual full automorphisms and their restrictions, plus all adjacency-pattern-matched partial injections, agrees for eight pairs and recovers the stated K_{3,2} polynomials.
residual_risks: The opening phrase 'all bijections between vertex-induced subgraphs' must be read as induced-subgraph isomorphisms, as explicitly defined in the scope and used in the proof. Finite tests are not the all-size proof.

evidence: The 9ed7bdcfaad0 catalog statement: 'For a finite equivalence relation whose occurring class sizes have minimum positive gap δ, every partial symmetry missing fewer than δ points extends to a full automorphism; the first nonextendible rank is exactly n−δ. A sharp factorial–binomial formula counts every map at this boundary, and paired finite generating formulas enumerate all partial maps and all extendible ones in every rank.'
For the size list (a,b), the positive gap is δ=a−b, so the boundary n−δ is 2b. No equal-size assumption excludes this case.

evidence: The equivalence-class matching for two classes has only the preserving orientation and the swapping orientation, omitting empty sides. In the preserving orientation ordinary rook factors give R_aR_b. For the swap the two rectangular rook factors are 1+C, with the all-empty intersection removed, so subtracting the extension polynomial gives C(C+2). The rank support and boundary coefficient follow immediately from these factors.

value.rationale: Global extension obstructions are a meaningful invariant, and the factored biclique formula is a useful example. As a standalone contribution, however, it is a direct complement translation and two-class reduction of an already indexed full rank-and-extension classification. The factorization is the routine product of two independent partial matchings; no independent extremal phenomenon or refined invariant survives this comparison.
residual_risks: Rejection as a finding does not dispute the correctness or pedagogical usefulness of the example.
